critical_code_review_comments: test_prize_board.py originally had TWO test classes (CRUD + Spin). With pytest.ini pinned to `-n 2 --dist loadscope`, xdist put the classes on DIFFERENT workers, so the CRUD-class module-fixture teardown (restore defaults) raced against the Spin-class autouse `_set_board`. Product code was fine; only the tests were racy. Consolidated into a single TestPrizeBoard class (fixture scope=class, explicit _reset_test_board() before spin tests). 8/8 now green across 5 consecutive runs.
spin() correctly reads the persisted board (`state_get('prize_board', DEFAULT)`) on every call, pops posCode from public response, stores it on the redemption doc for staff-side lookup — clean.
Prize Board input validation is server-enforced: label trimmed + capped 60 chars, posCode capped 24 chars, <2 good prizes → 400, blank dud label → 400. Verified via curl.
server.py continues to grow (>2900 lines). Splitting into modules (maximizer/, auth/, reports/, scheduler/) still recommended — carried over from prior iterations.

rca of the issue: Root cause (test-only): pytest.ini uses `-n 2 --dist loadscope` which distributes by scope (class here). The two prize_board test classes ran on different xdist workers and shared MongoDB state. TestPrizeBoardCrud's teardown restored defaults concurrently with TestSpinUsesBoard's autouse `_set_board` on the other worker, so the spin call intermittently saw the DEFAULT board (10% Off dud) instead of TEST_BOARD (TEST Candy Bar). Fix: merged both classes into a single TestPrizeBoard class so all 8 tests execute serially on ONE worker, with per-test `_reset_test_board()` guaranteeing state right before each spin/redeem check. Verified 5 consecutive full-file runs = 8 passed.
